children: Ford Motor Co. (F, Financials) is raising the bar for its new Fathom electric vehicle, with reports suggesting a goal of more than 100,000 U.S. sales in its first year available.
That's a tough standard. No other carmaker has sold more than 100,000 of a single EV model in the U.S. in one year. Ford is betting that price can change that.

Pricing for the Fathom is planned to start around $30,000, making it a candidate for buyers who may otherwise shop for a gasoline or hybrid vehicle. Ford executives have maintained the vehicle appeals to a far larger swath than the typical EV buyer.

That might make Fathom even more crucial than a different model introduction. Ford has been striving for years to make its EV business work at scale, and a lower-cost truck provides it an opportunity to prove that volume doesn't have to come with even larger losses.
There is still a lot to prove. Ford's U.S. sales were down 10.3% in August. Demand would have to be much higher than what most non-Tesla EVs have accomplished to get to 100,000 Fathom sales.
The next test comes early next year, when Ford starts collecting orders and investors receive their first true sense of demand.

title: Ford's $30,000 EV Is Chasing a Sales Milestone Only Tesla Has Reached
